title: Razor Runtime Compilation Obsolete
description: Learn why Razor runtime compilation is obsolete in .NET 10 and how to migrate to Razor compilation with Hot Reload or pre-compiled views.

data.text: Razor runtime compilation allowed .cshtml files to be compiled on-the-fly at runtime. This was useful during development because changes to views were reflected immediately without restarting the application. However, it introduced overhead, security considerations, and complexity that are no longer necessary with modern tooling.

Hot Reload in .NET 10 provides a superior development experience: it updates running code and Razor views instantly without requiring runtime compilation infrastructure. Hot Reload is faster, more reliable, and works across the full application stack — not just views. Additionally, runtime compilation introduced a surface area for security vulnerabilities that is best eliminated in production.

data.title: Breaking Change: Remove RCL Dependencies
data.text: If your project references Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Razor.RuntimeCompilation, you will see a build warning. The package is marked obsolete and may be removed in a future release.

To enable Hot Reload for Razor views, ensure you are running in the Development environment and using Visual Studio 2022 or later, or VS Code with the .NET Hot Reload extension. Hot Reload is enabled by default in modern .NET project templates.

data.title: Hot Reload is enabled by default in .NET 10
data.content: No additional configuration is needed — just run the app in Development mode

data.text: For production deployments, use pre-compiled views. The .NET SDK compiles .cshtml files into the assembly during build, eliminating the need for runtime compilation. This improves startup performance and removes the risk of runtime compilation errors.

data.title: Enable pre-compiled views in the project file
data.content: Configure the project to pre-compile Razor views at build time

data.title: Migration Steps
items: Remove calls to AddRazorRuntimeCompilation() from Program.cs.
Enable Hot Reload in your IDE for development-time view updates.
Enable pre-compiled views via RazorCompileOnBuild for production builds.
Verify that views render correctly after the migration.

data.title: Summary
points: Razor runtime compilation is obsolete in .NET 10.
Hot Reload replaces runtime compilation for development workflows.
Pre-compiled views are the recommended production approach.
Remove the RuntimeCompilation package and related configuration.
data.takeaway: The move away from runtime compilation simplifies the ASP.NET Core deployment model and encourages a cleaner separation between development and production view handling.
